headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q2 RECORD FCF: $1.6B NET EARNINGS, $625M TO SHAREHOLDERS — 855,816 oz at $4,483/oz Avg (TSX/NYSE: AEM)
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines released Q2 2026 results on July 29 featuring record quarterly free cash flow, net income of $1,600.5 million ($1.54/share adjusted), and $625 million returned to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in a single quarter — the largest distribution in company history. Production of 855,816 ounces at an average realized price of $4,483/oz translated into first-half operating cash flow of $3,490 million, lifting the balance sheet to a net cash position of $3,267 million. Full-year guidance held at the low end of 3.3–3.5 million ounces. For retail investors watching how $4,000+ gold translates into mining company economics, Agnico Eagle's Q2 is the benchmark case: disciplined cost control at scale generating free cash flow that has nowhere to go but dividends, buybacks, and selective exploration — including the first Hope Bay drill campaign since acquiring the asset in 2021.

headline: G MINING CLOSES G2 GOLDFIELDS — Combines Oko West + Oko-Ghanie for 500koz/yr Guyana Gold Hub (TSX: GMIN)
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) completed its acquisition of G2 Goldfields Inc. on July 29, 2026, under a plan of arrangement that also spun out G3 Goldfields Inc. to G2 shareholders. Each G2 share was exchanged for 0.212 GMIN shares plus 0.50 G3 shares. The combination consolidates two adjacent projects in Guyana's Oko corridor: GMIN's fully permitted and financed Oko West Mine with G2's Oko-Ghanie Project, creating what the companies describe as one of the largest, lowest-cost gold mining hubs in the Americas with life-of-mine average production potential exceeding 500,000 ounces per year. This is the second major gold M&A closing in three days — Equinox/Orla closed July 31 — and both reflect the same thesis: at $4,000+ gold, scale and cost structure matter more than optionality.

headline: HUDBAY Q2: $1.3B TRAILING EBITDA, COPPER COSTS AT -$0.40/lb — $631M Revenue; 2026 Cost Guidance Improved (TSX/NYSE: HBM)
snippet: Hudbay Minerals reported Q2 2026 revenue of $631.3 million, adjusted EBITDA of $321.2 million, and net earnings of $137.4 million, bringing the trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA to a record $1.3 billion. Industry-leading consolidated cash costs of -$0.40/lb copper (gold byproduct credit drives this below zero) and sustaining costs of $1.39/lb set the sector benchmark for copper-gold diversification at $6.29/lb copper. The company improved its 2026 consolidated cash cost guidance to -$0.45 to -$0.25/lb copper, ended the quarter with $1.04 billion in liquidity, and flipped to negative net debt of $80.5 million. Q2 copper production of 28,267 tonnes and gold of 51,234 ounces demonstrated the value of diversified copper-gold assets in the current commodity environment — this is the operational leverage case for copper-focused juniors in concrete numbers.

headline: COMMERZBANK CUTS GOLD TARGET TO $4,500/oz — Silver to $67; First Wall Street Downgrade in 11 Quarters
snippet: Commerzbank on July 28 cut its year-end 2026 gold price forecast by $300 to $4,500/oz (from $4,800) and lowered its silver target to $67/oz from $80/oz, marking the first time in eleven consecutive quarters that a major Wall Street bank has downgraded gold's outlook. The bank cited higher real yields, a hawkish Federal Reserve with two voting members dissenting in favour of a July rate hike, and Middle East tensions that are failing to sustain a safe-haven premium as drivers of the revision. Despite the cut, Commerzbank still sees gold recovering to $5,000/oz by end-2027 if the Fed holds rates and eventually pivots — making the downgrade a timing call rather than a structural one. For junior mining investors, the practical implication is that the re-rating of gold equities is delayed, not cancelled.

headline: CHINA BLACKLISTS RHEINMETALL + 13 EU FIRMS FROM RARE EARTHS — Magnets, Dysprosium, Terbium in Beijing's Retaliation
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce on July 24 added 14 European entities — including Rheinmetall AG, Tatra Trucks, Lafert S.p.A., InPACT S.A., and Vigo Photonics — to its export control list, prohibiting the transfer of dual-use materials including rare earths (scandium, yttrium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium), gallium, germanium, graphite, antimony, tungsten, and permanent magnets without special authorization. The ban carries extraterritorial reach: no organization anywhere in the world may transfer Chinese-origin dual-use goods to listed entities. Beijing moved list-for-list within 24 hours of the EU's 21st Russia sanctions package on July 23. The targeted companies include defense manufacturers and advanced tech suppliers — the exact customers that Western rare earth mine-to-magnet producers are trying to serve, and the clearest possible signal that supply chain independence from China is not optional.

headline: BANYAN GOLD NITRA FIRST HOLE: 17.8 g/t AU IN NEW YUKON ZONE — Roaring Fork Discovery 25km from AurMac (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) released results on July 28 from its first two drillholes at the Nitra Gold Project in the Mayo Mining District, Yukon — 25 kilometres west of the AurMac Deposit. Hole NT-26-001 at the newly identified Roaring Fork zone returned 1.62 g/t Au over 5.0 metres including a high-grade core of 17.80 g/t Au over 0.4 metres, while hole NT-26-006 confirmed visible gold and bismuth-sulphosalt mineralization in quartz veins at the Seattle Creek zone. These are the first of eleven exploration targets in a 7,500-metre greenfields program across Banyan's 830 sq km land package; claims are 100% owned with no underlying royalties. The Nitra results have identified a potential new gold system in the same camp as AurMac (2.1 million ounces at 1.13 g/t in the 2024 resource) before a single dollar of exploration capital was committed to this ground.

headline: MOROCCO STRATEGIC: 14.88% CU, 696 g/t AG AT OUNEINE — Plus 4.16 g/t Au at Second Target; Anti-Atlas (TSXV: MCC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Morocco Strategic Minerals
snippet: Morocco Strategic Minerals Corp. (TSXV: MCC) reported Phase 1 surface sampling results on July 29 from its Anti-Atlas properties in Morocco: at Ouneine, 49 grab samples returned values up to 14.88% copper and 696 g/t silver, with 37 of 49 samples exceeding 1.0% Cu and 8 exceeding 5.29% Cu. At the Aït Zekri target, 23 grab samples returned up to 4.16 g/t gold at surface and 2.11 g/t Au from underground gallery. MCC holds an option to acquire 80% of a district-scale package of five exploitation licenses and two research permits, with environmental authorization in place for a central flotation plant. Grab samples are not representative of average grade but they confirm the presence of a high-grade multi-metal system in a jurisdiction with established mining infrastructure — and the grades are exceptional.

headline: FIREFLY METALS GREEN BAY: 9.8m @ 16.5% CuEq IN VMS CORE — Early Production Case Building; PEA Due August (TSX: FFM)
snippet: FireFly Metals Ltd. (TSX/ASX: FFM) released Q2 2026 operational highlights on July 27 from its multi-rig underground drilling campaign at the Green Bay Copper-Gold Project in Newfoundland, with headline intercepts of 42.0 metres at 6.1% CuEq including a Volcanogenic Massive Sulphide core of 9.8 metres at 16.5% CuEq, and 51.5 metres at 4.9% CuEq including 17.0 metres at 9.1% CuEq. The company is well-funded with approximately A$196 million in cash and liquid investments, and its Preliminary Economic Assessment is on track for completion in August 2026. VMS deposits at these grades are among the highest-returning copper assets in the world — and Green Bay is still being defined. The PEA in August will be the first opportunity to put economics on what the drilling is showing.

headline: PANORO COTABAMBAS: SECOND RIG DRILLING — 45,000m Peru Cu-Au Porphyry on 317m @ 1.04% CuEq Base Case (TSXV: PML)
snippet: Panoro Minerals Ltd. (TSXV: PML) provided a July 27 update confirming a second drill rig is operating at the South Pit of its 100%-owned Cotabambas Copper, Gold and Silver Project in Apurimac, Peru, as part of a 45,000-metre program targeting high-grade mineralization along a 3-kilometre strike between the North and South Pits. The company plans to operate five rigs by end of Q3 2026. Previous drilling returned a base-case intercept of 317.6 metres at 1.04% CuEq — the kind of thickness and grade that copper porphyry resource models are built on. At $6.29/lb copper and with the US tariff framework temporarily exempting refined copper through year-end, Apurimac copper porphyry economics have rarely been stronger, and Panoro is drilling aggressively while the window is open.

headline: SLVP +69% vs GLD +22% IN ONE YEAR — Motley Fool Makes the Case for Silver Mining Stocks Over Gold Bullion in 2026
snippet: Motley Fool's July 28 comparison of GLD (SPDR Gold Shares) versus SLVP (iShares MSCI Global Silver and Metals Miners ETF) finds that silver mining stocks outperformed gold bullion by 47 percentage points in the trailing year — 69% vs 22% — and makes the case for SLVP as the preferred exposure for 2026. The analysis cites three advantages: dividend income (SLVP pays a yield; GLD does not), M&A activity benefiting portfolio companies, and operational leverage to silver's structural supply deficit (sixth consecutive year, 46.3 million ounce shortfall projected for 2026). GLD's lower volatility — maximum drawdown 26% vs SLVP's 48% — remains the argument for risk-averse holders, but for retail investors with a longer horizon, the mining equity overlay has historically amplified the metals move when the cycle turns.
